small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_M configs (M=128 covers full batch in 1 row-tile) with BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32/64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4; with BATCH=128 the current BLOCK_M=16/32 oversubscribes row tiles and wastes L2 reuse on weight columns.
- Drop GROUP_M swizzle (only 1-2 row groups exist at BLOCK_M≥64) and instead iterate pid along the N axis to maximize x-row reuse; also try BLOCK_K=32 with num_stages=5 to deepen the K-pipeline.
- Cast weight (and optionally x) to fp16/bf16 before stage1 to enable real tensor-core tf16 `tl.dot` throughput on Ada — fp32×fp32 tf32 on 4090 caps far below fp16 tensor cores; correctness tol 5e-2 easily allows it.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a "split-K, fused-everything" single kernel: one program per (M-tile of rows, N-tile of pooled outputs), load the X row tile once into SRAM, stream weight K-slabs, compute the GEMM tile, fuse bias+pool+partial-sum-over-pooled-N inside the epilogue, and atomic-add the scalar partial into out[m]. This eliminates the 128×16384 pooled materialization entirely.
- Store weight in fp16 (or bf16) in a persistent buffer at init and run `tl.dot` in fp16 with fp32 accumulator — this is the single biggest lever on a 4090 for a 128×32768×32768 GEMM; current fp32 path is compute-bound at TF32 rates.
- Consider a persistent-CTA design sized to SM count (128 SMs on 4090): each CTA loops over assigned (m,n_pool) tiles, keeping x rows resident across multiple N tiles for maximal reuse of the 128-row activation block.
